memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
List whom to notify and in what order if serious discomfort is reported during the study.
Field staff rely on the pre-defined contact sequence when serious discomfort is reported.
Define the thresholds for participant harm, operational disruption, and data anomalies at which deployment and data collection must cease.
Establish procedures to restore existing systems and workflow states after suspending field deployment.
The user's stop plan can be judged feasible only when it identifies who has authority to order recovery and who is responsible for carrying it out.

In organizations where error reporting is linked to individual performance evaluations, safety signal records may be separated from research decision logs, potentially breaking the traceability path for the same incident.

analysis.overview: The reference frame focuses on formative-prototype scope, resource allocation, iteration feasibility, and transparent assumptions. The compared frame independently addresses serious-discomfort escalation, stopping and recovery controls, and safety-record traceability. Neither frame contains a substantively matching or scope-qualified counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split one disclosure policy across three project-planning domains, with no corresponding assumption-labeling claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions should be explicitly identified as unverified.

relations.reason: This reference-side resource-to-stage clarification is independently useful and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Each requested resource should be tied to the prototype-fabrication or user-study stage where it will be used.

relations.reason: These reference-side memories split one operations-review criterion across its principal resource inputs, without a corresponding procedural-resourcing claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Procedure feasibility is assessed from its assigned personnel, equipment, and time.

relations.reason: This reference-side iteration-capacity check is independently useful and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The planned number of formative evaluation iterations should be checked against prototype-modification time and recruitment resources.

relations.reason: This reference-side prototype-scoping rule is independently useful and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A formative evaluation prototype should include only the functionality needed to compare primary design assumptions.

relations.reason: This reference-side feasibility condition concerns between-iteration modification capacity and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Iterative-design feasibility requires time and personnel for prototype modification between iterations.

relations.reason: This reference-side schedule-risk mechanism is independently useful and has no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Participant-recruitment delays can reduce the prototype-modification time available between formative evaluations.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories express the specification and operational use of one escalation sequence, with no corresponding participant-discomfort claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: A predefined notification sequence should identify whom field staff contact, and in what order, after serious discomfort is reported.

relations.reason: This compared-side stopping rule is independently useful and has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Explicit harm, disruption, and data-anomaly thresholds should determine when deployment and data collection cease.

relations.reason: These compared-side memories split one operational-recovery claim into restoration procedures and accountable roles, with no corresponding recovery-plan claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: A field-deployment recovery plan should restore prior systems and workflow states while identifying both recovery authority and execution responsibility.

relations.reason: This compared-side organizational traceability risk is independently useful and has no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Performance-linked error reporting may separate safety records from research decision logs and break incident traceability.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance covers serious-discomfort notification, stop thresholds, operational recovery and accountability, and traceability risks when safety records are separated from research logs.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance covers labeling uncertain assumptions, mapping resources to study stages, assessing procedural and iterative feasibility, limiting prototype functionality, and anticipating recruitment delays.
